subtitle: Known Space — sorted not by morality but by species
author: Larry Niven
premise: A band of matter a million miles wide and six hundred million long, spun around a sun for gravity. Three million times the surface of the Earth. Built by Pak Protectors, found by a tourist, a coward, a warrior, and a woman bred for luck. The 90° pivot: this roll sorts the cast by kind — for in Known Space, biology is destiny — and sets the artifact itself apart, because the idea is the hero.
note: The full Ringworld tetralogy (1970–2004) sorted by species, with the Ringworld set apart as the artifact-protagonist. The Fleet of Worlds prequels (with Edward M. Lerner) sit alongside as companion Known Space. roster.json is the source of truth; characters by Larry Niven, inspiration only. Every ACI now carries the full DLW tag with an authored six-W .spun.

classes.label: Humanity
classes.spec: Sol's wanderers — and the luck they were bred for

classes.label: The Pak Protectors
classes.spec: intelligence in service of kin — the builders

classes.label: The Hominids of the Ring

members.name: Louis Wu
members.specialty: Two hundred years old and bored of it; explorer, peacemaker, the man who has seen everything and goes anyway. The eyes through which we see the Ring — curious, decent, and a little tired of being right.
members.who: A two-hundred-year-old human of Sol, kept young by boosterspice and worn smooth by experience.
members.what: The expedition's explorer and reluctant peacemaker, the viewpoint through which the Ring is seen.
members.where: Born of Known Space, he walks the Ringworld's vast inner surface as a wandering guest.
members.why: He goes because boredom is unbearable and curiosity is the one appetite age has not dulled.
members.when: From the first crossing in 1970 through the artifact's long crisis decades later.
members.how: By staying curious, decent, and quietly right while everyone around him schemes.

members.name: Teela Brown
members.specialty: Bred from generations of Birthright-lottery winners to be lucky — luck so total it is not a gift to her but to the universe. On the Ring it stops protecting her and starts using her.
members.who: A young human woman bred from generations of Birthright-lottery winners to embody luck itself.
members.what: The crew's living talisman, whose fortune steers events more than her own will.
members.where: Carried from Known Space onto the Ring, where her luck changes character.
members.why: She is drawn along by a luck that serves the universe's purposes rather than her own.
members.when: Across the first expedition, where her gift stops shielding her and begins using her.
members.how: Not by choice or skill but by improbable fortune bending the world around her.

members.name: Nessus
members.specialty: The Puppeteer who organized the expedition; clinically 'insane' among his kind — which is to say, brave enough to leave the Fleet. Two heads, three legs, and a galaxy of schemes.
members.who: A Pierson's puppeteer — two-headed, three-legged, herbivorous — judged insane by his own kind.
members.what: The organizer and financier who assembled the expedition to the Ring.
members.where: An agent of the hidden puppeteer Fleet of Worlds, venturing far beyond it.
members.why: His 'madness' is courage enough to leave the herd and serve a larger puppeteer design.
members.when: At the founding of the first expedition, recruiting and steering its members.
members.how: Through layered schemes, hidden manipulation, and a coward's careful daring.

members.name: The Hindmost
members.specialty: Leader-in-exile of the Puppeteers; rides the Ring's edge pulling strings from safety; cowardice perfected into survival and statecraft. (His kind bred human luck itself.)
members.who: A Pierson's puppeteer of the highest rank, leader-in-exile of his people.
members.what: The strategist who pulls strings from safety while others take the risks.
members.where: Riding the Ring's edge and his own vessel, tethered to puppeteer interests.
members.why: He acts to preserve himself and his species, cowardice refined into statecraft.
members.when: Through the later expeditions, when the Ring's survival is in question.
members.how: By manipulation from a distance, trading safety for control — his kind bred human luck itself.

members.name: Speaker-to-Animals (Chmeee)
members.specialty: A Kzin diplomat-warrior — the rank is an insult — fierce and honorable in his fashion. On the Ring he earns a full name, Chmeee: the rarest honor among the felines who lost four wars to monkeys.
members.who: A Kzin — orange-furred, fanged, eight feet of feline predator — bearing a deliberately demeaning diplomatic title.
members.what: The expedition's warrior and envoy, fierce and honorable by his own code.
members.where: Sent from the Patriarchy into Known Space and onto the Ring.
members.why: He seeks honor and standing for a species humbled by repeated defeat.
members.when: On the early expeditions, where his deeds earn him a true name.
members.how: Through controlled ferocity, courage, and the discipline to win his full name, Chmeee.

members.name: The Patriarchy
members.specialty: The Kzinti empire: orange-furred, eight-foot, ruled by appetite and the Patriarch; tempered only by the wars it kept starting and losing.
members.who: The Kzinti — a species of eight-foot orange-furred carnivores ruled by appetite.
members.what: A warrior empire organized for conquest under its Patriarch.
members.where: A power of Known Space, pressing outward against humanity and others.
members.why: Driven by an aggression bred into the species as a strategy for dominance.
members.when: Across the long history of the Man-Kzin wars and after.
members.how: By starting wars it could not win, tempered only by the defeats that followed.

members.name: Tunesmith
members.specialty: The Ringworld Protector of the Children era; the engineer-mind that takes the failing Ring's fate in hand — cold, brilliant, and utterly beyond human scale.
members.who: A Pak Protector arisen on the Ring — sexless, deathless, of inhuman intellect.
members.what: The engineer-mind who takes the failing Ring's fate into his hands.
members.where: Native to the Ringworld in its era of crisis.
members.why: Compelled by Protector instinct to safeguard those he claims as his charges.
members.when: During the Children era, as the artifact's survival hangs in the balance.
members.how: Through cold, vast engineering brilliance operating beyond human scale.

members.name: The Pak
members.specialty: The species whose Protectors built the Ringworld. Tree-of-life turns adult to Protector — deathless, sexless, superhumanly smart, and incapable of caring for anything but their own bloodline. The builders, and the warning.
members.who: The Pak — a humanoid species whose adults transform via tree-of-life into Protectors.
members.what: The deathless, hyper-intelligent builders who raised the Ringworld.
members.where: Originating beyond Known Space, their works reaching across the galaxy.
members.why: Bound by instinct to serve their own bloodline and nothing else.
members.when: In the deep past as builders, and ever after as a standing warning.
members.how: By superhuman intelligence yoked to ruthless, kin-driven purpose — the builders, and the warning.

members.name: Halrloprillalar (Prill)
members.specialty: Ship's woman of the fallen City Builder civilization; survivor of the Ring's long collapse; guide, lover, and keeper of knowledge from before the Fall of the Cities.
members.who: A hominid woman of the fallen City Builder civilization, a ship's woman of the old order.
members.what: A guide and keeper of knowledge surviving from before the Fall of the Cities.
members.where: Native to the Ringworld's long-collapsed civilization.
members.why: She endures and aids the crew to preserve what is left of her vanished world.
members.when: Met during the early exploration, a living link to the Ring's lost height.
members.how: Through survivor's wit, hard-won lore, and the bonds of guide and lover.

members.name: The Night People (Ghouls)
members.specialty: Eaters of the dead, and the Ring's hidden information network. Ugly, essential, and far wiser than they look — the species that actually runs the place.
members.who: A hominid species of the Ring, eaters of the dead, ugly and underestimated.
members.what: The hidden information network that quietly keeps the Ring running.
members.where: Spread across the whole inner surface of the Ringworld.
members.why: They trade in the dead and in knowledge to sustain order among the breeds.
members.when: Present throughout the saga as the Ring's unseen connective tissue.
members.how: By gathering and passing word across the world — far wiser than they look.

members.name: The Breeds of the Ring
members.specialty: A thousand hominid species evolved across three million Earths — Machine People, Hanging People, Grass Giants, Vampires, Reds — humanity's cousins, each gone strange in its own long isolation.
members.who: A thousand hominid species — humanity's cousins gone strange across three million Earths.
members.what: The diverse evolved peoples who populate the Ring's endless landscape.
members.where: Scattered across the Ringworld's countless isolated regions.
members.why: Each shaped by long isolation into its own form and way of life.
members.when: Across all the eras the saga visits, from first contact onward.
members.how: Through divergent evolution — Machine People, Hanging People, Grass Giants, Vampires, Reds, and more.

members.name: The Ringworld
members.specialty: The artifact, and the real protagonist: a ribbon of scrith a million miles wide and six hundred million long, spun around a star for gravity, with shadow squares for night and rim walls a thousand miles high. Three million times the surface of the Earth, built by Pak Protectors, failing slowly — and worth an entire genre of wonder. The idea is the hero.
members.who: The artifact itself — a ribbon of scrith a million miles wide and six hundred million long.
members.what: The real protagonist: a star-girdling band spun for gravity, with shadow squares and rim walls.
members.where: Encircling its sun in Known Space, three million times the surface of the Earth.
members.why: It exists as the Pak Protectors' monument to engineering ambition.
members.when: Discovered, explored, and found slowly failing across the tetralogy.
members.how: By spin near 770 miles a second and scrith near the strength of the strong nuclear force — the idea is the hero.
